chapter: Brass band and the Lyric Theater
title: The Lyric Theater band under John Robichaux and Midnight Rambles
summary: The Lyric band played jazz for vaudeville shows, led by Professor Robichaux; he describes the theater, rehearsals, Midnight Rambles and late dances.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I was asking about the band at the Lyric Theater. What kind of a band it was, what they did there? Boy, at the Lyric Theater, they had a wonderful band over there. They used to play for the shows. And they had Andrew Kimball was playing trumpet. And Margaret Kimball, his wife, was playing piano. And they had Johnny Lindsay was playing trombone. And Red Happy was playing drum. And Lurie Nelson was playing clarinet. And old man John Robichaud, he was playing violin. He was the leader? He was the leader. Did they play anything like overtures or just for the shows or different acts? Well, no. They mostly played jazz. Jazz. Jazz. Jazz. No more. They mostly played jazz. No more. Did they read any? Oh, yeah. Yeah. Did they play for the movies or any? Did they have movies in those days? Yeah, they had music. Yeah, they had music. I mean the movie, motion pictures, did they play for those? No, they didn't play for motion pictures. They played for the vortical. Just the vortical. Yeah, the vortical. Just the vortical. Did they read everything or did they just read part of it? Well, no. They read all the orchestration supposed to be wrote. But I mean lots of times they played fake numbers like the average musician does. No. But I know one thing, they had really a good orchestra and not only that. They had a man behind them, Professor Robichaud. He was wonderful. Because that was, that was, I played with him when he died, way before he died. I played about five years with him. And he'd make us come to rehearsal tonight and we got a job for tomorrow night. He wouldn't bring the same kind of music we played that day. He brought some other kind of music. And when he put it before, he said, what? We ain't seen it before. He said, what? You called yourself a musician? Well, we gonna play that tonight. What he rehearsed, he wouldn't play it on the job the next night. He'd bring something else. He'd say, yeah, you call yourself a musician? Play that night. Oh, there at the Lyric, did you play, did they play in a pit or did they ever play a number? Yeah, a pit. Did they ever play up on the stage too for special numbers or anything? No, no. They played in a pit. How big a place was that theater? That's torn down. I never did see that. Well, the theater was about, about bigger. That house on the end of this, this house on the end. I wondered how many, would it seat a couple of thousand you think maybe or something? About 1,500 people. 1,500 maybe? Yeah, about 1,500 people. Was that all colored? That was just far colored? All colored. All colored. Sure. That's where Bessie Smith and, uh, I couldn't tell you about it. Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith, all those girls used to come down there. Yeah. Did you ever play in that band? Yeah. At the theater too? Yeah, I played in the same theater. I was busy. Sorry, we can stop in. Sorry. Well, we were talking about the Lyric Theater. Yeah. How late did that run? Do you know when that closed down? Well, about, uh, 10.30. 9.30, 10.30. No, I meant though in years. Well, you mean the band or what? No, the whole theater. How long did the, how late did that last? Did they tear it down or burn down or what happened to it? I never did know. They tore it down. Tore it down. Yeah, tore it down. When was that? During the Depression about or when do you know? Oh yeah, it was, yeah, yeah, it was before Depression. Before Depression. Before Depression. Before Depression. Did you play Midnight Rambles there? Oh yeah, I played with John Robichaud over there. Yeah, I played with, I played with the band himself. And you played Midnight Rambles, huh? Yeah, yeah. How did that work? Well, you see, after the show, then they had what they call a ramble. In other words, a Midnight Rambles is just like everybody gathering in a place. No playing out. And they're like a jubilee or something like that. Yeah. That's what they were. Late, huh? Yeah. After the show. After the show. Now, lots of times we'd have jobs. After the show we'd go play over at the La Luziana restaurant. Oh yeah. John Robichaud used to have all that kind of way. Used to have all that. Would that be a special dinner, banquet or something? Yeah. A special dance. Dance? Yeah, a special dance.
